newsitem.title: FRANCE: France criticises EU farm reform plans.
newsitem.headline: France criticises EU farm reform plans.

text.p: France criticised on Wednesday a European Commission plan for further price-cutting farm reform, saying it would weaken rather than boost the EU's bargaining position in the next round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) trade talks.

The plan to lower EU farm price support towards world levels and shift agriculture support to direct payments to farmers might also prove costly and disadvantage some farm sectors, the farm ministry said in a statement.
France said it would carefully review the plan and consult farm organisations before deciding on the position it would defend in future negotiations with its EU partners.

The proposals, known as Agenda 2000, were unveiled on Wednesday in Strasbourg by European Commission President Jacques Santer. They are aimed at preparing the EU expansion eastwards and at preventing the return of costly food surpluses.
Santer told the European parliament that cuts in support prices would strengthen the EU's position in the next round of global WTO farm negotiations due to start in 1999.

But the French farm ministry said that by making voluntary prices cuts ahead of talks the EU might be forced into making further concessions to its trade partners on farm import tariffs or on the terms for access to EU markets.
"This strategy cannot be accepted as such by France and also by EU ministers," it said.

"I therefore claim the right before starting a detailed technical review of that project to assess it and discuss it in depth with representatives of the French farm world in order to define the position France will defend in European negotiations," the statement quoted minister Louis Le Pensec as saying.
France wanted a future accord on the EU farm reform plan to ensure that public aid would be fairly spread among farmers and that rural development and jobs were enhanced.
Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will meet later in the day with Luc Guyau, the head of France's largest farm union FNSEA, to discuss the EU plan, FNSEA officials said.
